thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: autopager triggered for node-nodepool-gpu-37 (zone us-west2-a) — kernel OOPS detected, kubelet NotReady. Pager: PagerDuty -> page fired to oncall tier1. Reason: kernel_oops + kubelet_unready + watchdog_reboot_count>3. Logs: /var/log/kern.log: 'BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference'
pagerduty: PagerDuty alert: INC-2026-48321 auto-generated. Severity: P2. Service: gpu-node-health. Notes: esc level=1, runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-node-kernel-oops
alyssa_oncall: acked via PagerDuty — I'm on it. pulling serial console and attaching.
jordan_oncall: thanks — grabbing kube events for pods in that node, will check tenant impact.
samir_infra: copy — I see the node reported nvram/memory errors earlier, possible driver panic. boot log attached in case.
maria_sre: tagging tenant-impact team. Any 5xxs or degraded endpoints? console shows kubelet heartbeat lost at 12:01:14 UTC.
alyssa_oncall: attaching serial dump excerpt:

```
[   14.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=0, GPU has fallen off the bus
[   14.123789] kernel: BUG: kernel NULL pointer deref in nvme_core_read()
[   14.124000] kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: Attempted to kill init!
```

alyssa_oncall: node went into Kernel panic then reboot loop. kubelet showed NotReady after reboot; kubelet log shows repeated SIGSEGV in nvidia driver.
jordan_oncall: tenant impact: observed 4 tenants with active jobs pinned to that node; autoscaler attempted to reschedule but taint prevented immediate schedule (gpu-alloc exclusive). I've opened a reschedule job to shift pods.
samir_infra: recommend cordon + drain then emergency instance replace. We'll need serial RMA if it's HW. I'll start a parallel validation on sibling hosts to ensure not systemic.
incident-bot: automated action: cordon node-nodepool-gpu-37 at 12:05:02 UTC. Drain initiated with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data flag.
alyssa_oncall: drain in progress. running:

```
kubectl cordon node-nodepool-gpu-37
kubectl drain node-nodepool-gpu-37 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

maria_sre: noticed a small bump in 503s on the embeddings endpoint from a single region; Routing flagged and failover to dedicated capacity triggered automatically — no global outage.
jordan_oncall: logs from kube-controller show pods pending due to nodeSelector/gpu-count. I'm manually patching a couple of low-priority batch jobs to use fallback model variant (cpu-backed) to reduce customer impact.
alyssa_oncall: done patching two batch jobs. Also moved three inference pods via eviction with PodDisruptionBudget check.
samir_infra: NVMe SMART is showing reallocated sectors on the host — this could be disk related causing kernel panic cascade. I'll open a support ticket with the colocation partner and queue an RMA for the host. Starting live-monitor: perform 'ipmitool sel list' + check power cycles.
kevin_infra_lead: +1 on RMA, but before that let's ensure we drain gracefully and not trigger mass reschedules. If we see more than 5 nodes in the rack having similar errors, escalate to datacenter ops.
maria_sre: FYI, customer-impact assessment: 4 tenants affected, 2 customers reported increased latency but no error spike. I'm drafting a short status note for comms — will post to #incidents if confirmed.
alyssa_oncall: drain complete. kube reports all non-daemonset pods evicted. Scheduling new instances: autoscaler spun up two spare nodes; one succeeded, one failed due to insufficient quota in the region — fallback to multi-region routing triggered for a handful of requests.
jordan_oncall: coordinating with infra to mark this node for offline reprovision. Current plan: isolate, run memtest + nvme stress, reprovision image, test driver stack. If fails, RMA.
samir_infra: running memtest now. Also I've pulled dmesg and pushed to the incident storage: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/4212349876/node-gpu-37-dmesg.txt
incident-bot: escalation policy check: node still in fail state >15m? escalate to tier2 infra.
alyssa_oncall: ACK — bringing kevin into the thread. @kevin_infra_lead tagging for RMA approval and quota bump for replacement.
kevin_infra_lead: I'm in. Approve RMA if memtest fails. I'll also request temporary quota increase for us-west2-a to avoid future fallback.
maria_sre: status note draft: "We are investigating a hardware-related failure in a GPU host in us-west2. Some in-region inference traffic experienced limited latency increases and partial failover to dedicated capacity. No global service impact. On-call is actively mitigating; RMA/repair in progress." Anyone want to adjust wording?
jordan_oncall: looks good. Add ETA: 2-4 hours for full RMA and reprovisioning.
alyssa_oncall: memtest results: several bit flips reported, running full suite — probable memory or board issue. NVMe results still concerning. Recommend RMA.
samir_infra: confirmed memtest errors. Initiating RMA and marking image for reprovision after swap. I also set a quick probe to detect similar signatures on sibling hosts.
incident-bot: PagerDuty note: INC-2026-48321 status updated -> acknowledged by alyssa_oncall, escalated to infra (kevin_infra_lead). Incident severity remains P2. Add timeline and tags: kernel_oops, nvme, gpu-host.
alyssa_oncall: handing off follow-ups to samir and kevin (infra leads) for RMA and reprovision sequencing. I'll monitor customer impact and update status messages. If any customer escalates, page me directly.
kevin_infra_lead: I'll take the handoff for hardware and RMA. Samir, coordinate the swap and verify network config post-swap. Maria, please push the incident note to #incidents with current ETA.
maria_sre: status posted to #incidents. Reaction :white_check_mark:. I'll stay on watch for customer replies. Creating postmortem placeholder with initial timeline.
alyssa_oncall: thanks everyone. closing active paging loop from oncall side. leaving thread open for infra to update once RMA complete. :thumbsup:
samir_infra: will update thread with RMA ticket number and replacement host ID once available.
kevin_infra_lead: noted. Adding post-reprovision checklist: validate driver stack, run small batch infer test, run 1hr soak, then return to prod.
maria_sre: noted — adding to runbook. End of immediate responder actions. Followups: postmortem owner (alyssa_oncall), timeline, RCA owner (samir_infra).
